text:
Bitcoin retreated to $77,800 after tagging $81,000 highs, as Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh struck a decidedly hawkish tone in his debut Jackson Hole keynote. Warsh emphasized persistent services inflation above the 2% target, pushing market-implied odds of a September 16 rate hike to 57.5% from 35%.

The policy pivot paused a nine-day winning streak for U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, which nevertheless locked in over $3 billion in cumulative August net inflows led by BlackRock and Fidelity. As 10-year Treasury yields rebounded toward 3.92% and the U.S. Dollar Index firmed, equity benchmarks slipped alongside digital assets. This immediate co-movement underscores that crypto risk premia remain strictly tethered to central bank rate trajectories and sovereign yield curves, even as monthly institutional accumulation establishes a resilient structural baseline.
